newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Stevedores continue occupation at Brazil's Santos.
newsitem.headline: Stevedores continue occupation at Brazil's Santos.

text.p: Stevedores at Brazil's Santos port continued to occupy vessels at the terminal of steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) and but both sides refused to make any move that could trigger a strike.

Twenty-six stevedores remained aboard two vessels docked at Cosipa's private terminal at the port while military police observed from the pier. The occupation has effectively paralyzed all operations at the Cosipa terminal since last week.

The unions are protesting against a ruling which allows Cosipa to use its own workers to load and unload vessels at the terminal. Unions say only qualified and registered stevedores should be allowed to perform the operations.
The stevedores maintained their promise to start a strike at Santos should the steel firm attempt to load or unload any vessels at its terminal.
"There is no strike whatsoever except for the Cosipa terminal which is paralysed," said Abelardo Fernandes, president of the National Stevedores' Union. "The situation remains the same."
The port authority Codesp said there were three vessels waiting to dock at the Cosipa terminal, but the company had not notified the port of any docking.
"We have a daily meeting to discuss dockings," said a port spokesman. "The company doesn't want to request permission for the vessel to dock."

The Rio Trombetas was waiting to unload 52,000 tonnes iron ore. There were two other vessels waiting to dock at the Cosipa terminal, one to unload 28,000 tonnes iron ore and one to unload 38,900 tonnes coal.

Cosipa said it had obtained a judicial order last week to evacuate the stevedores from the vessel but the police had not enforced it yet. The company was studying whether to ask for army reinforcements to make sure the order was carried out.
